text: The ACE migration of this story keeps the legacy file name V027__rwb_ace_001_recovery_source_additions.sql and takes the next free version on the ACE schema's own Flyway sequence, allocated by the ACE DBA at build time; the story writes no version number of its own.
why: The sources fix the head at V026 and name the file V027, but the ACE schema is ACE's and its sequence owner allocates versions; DP-15 puts each migration on one owner's sequence, and here that owner is ACE.
read: Legacy RWB-ACE-001 sections 3 and 12; FSD P1 v3 A2.1; TSD P1 v3 T3.2
confirm: ACE team lead and ACE DBA at build time
impact: The version appears in the ACE release notes; no object, grant or test depends on the number.

text: The grantee of SELECT on the 14 new tables is the NOLOGIN role ace_view_owner, and the 12 new columns on account, customer and efs_action arrive inside the table-level SELECT that role already holds; no column-level grant is written and no service login receives a grant in schema public.
why: The legacy story names 'the view-owner role agreed with the Workbench environment design' and no role code; the target names one view owner for all 30 views (TSD P1 T6.3), and the 12 columns sit on tables that role already reads through the 16 Section A views.
read: Legacy RWB-ACE-001 AC4 and section 10; TSD P1 v3 T6.3; Architecture v5 slide 29
confirm: Recovery data architect and ACE DBA
impact: One role, one grant block; a second grantee or a column grant would be a finding in AceGrantCheck.

text: The 14 ACE ingestion jobs stay ACE Spring Batch jobs with ACE's own job names, interface numbers and cadence; this story writes no cadence, cut-off or interface number, and the batch record is the only schedule evidence it relies on.
why: Legacy section 12 says one Spring Batch job per source and the sources name no interface number or time; ACE owns ingest scheduling and the target moves only Workbench schedules to Temporal (DP-10).
read: Legacy RWB-ACE-001 sections 3 and 12; FSD P1 v3 A1.2 FEAT-RDF-03 to FEAT-RDF-06 removed; TSD P1 v3 T3.2
impact: No Temporal Schedule and no new timer is created for ACE ingestion; the jobs' numbers are named in the ACE run book, not here.

text: DL43, the ACE acceptance of the RWB-ACE-001 scope and dates, is treated as accepted for this run; the story proceeds in Draft status with no approval gate, and the Section B work of rwb-source-data (RWB-P1-E1069) waits until this story is reported done rather than on a signed decision.
why: The realignment run records a missing approval or status as an assumption and continues in Draft, and no human approval stop exists in this stage; FSD P1 v3 OQ-P1-01 still lists DL43 as open with a date of 2026-11-21.
read: FSD P1 v3 open points OQ-P1-01 and OQ-P1-02; legacy RWB-ACE-001 status line and section 3
confirm: ACE team lead and the Recovery programme board at DL43
impact: If DL43 is refused or its dates move, the release date of this story and of the 14 Section B views move with it; no object or test changes.

text: The two platform dependencies added by the applied patterns, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON for DP-15 and RWB-PLT-N001-CON for DP-19, are recorded as notes in section 13 and not in 'Depends on (build)', which the Work Package fixes as None; the ACE migration starts with neither, because the ACE schema and its sequence are ACE's own.
why: The Work Package fixes H, C, I and X as empty lists and the metadata table copies them exactly; the DP table adds the platform dependency as a pattern rule, so the reading is recorded where it is applied.
read: Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-15 and DP-19; Work Package B2-P1-003 story line for RWB-P1-ACE001-DB
confirm: Coordinator at stage C when the lane and the Day-1 allocation are assembled
impact: The lane reads Day 1; if the coordinator later adds the platform CON dependency, only the fragment and the metadata row change.
